terms.gloss: a degree of comparison: positive, comparative, superlative
terms.comment: The positive is gradus positīvus, the comparative comparātīvus, the superlative superlātīvus (Traupman 232, 246); the question is Cujus gradūs comparātiōnis est? (244); “in the comparative” is in comparātiōne or comparātīvē. Gradus, a step or degree, and comparātiō are classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase in Lewis & Short. Positīvus of the positive degree is in the late grammarian Cledonius (Lewis & Short; Gellius uses the word of names fixed by convention). Quintilian speaks of comparatives and superlatives as comparātiōnēs et superlātiōnēs (1.5.45, Lewis & Short s.v. superlātiō).

phrases.latin: Quot gradūs comparātiōnis sunt adjectīvīs? — Trēs gradūs comparātiōnis.
phrases.english: How many degrees of comparison do adjectives have? — Three degrees of comparison.
What degree of comparison is it? — The positive.

sources: Lewis & Short: gradus · Lewis & Short: comparatio · Lewis & Short: positivus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 232, 244, 246, 248, 294, 302.
